subject: Throughput squeeze — customer-level throttling; board/customer flag
participants_external: laura@healthsync.com (Laura Nguyen, Head of Platform, HealthSync)
messages:
From: Laura Nguyen <laura@healthsync.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: support@healthsync.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production throttling impacting inference pipelines (urgent)

Olga — we started seeing sustained 429s and p95 latency >1.8s across our inference batches since 06:40 PDT. This correlates with our heavy nightly batch fan-out. We're fully blocked on two critical features and the CFO is asking for an immediate remediation plan.

Quick facts:
- Error rate: ~12% 429/5xx for tenant healthsync-prod between 06:40–08:50 PDT
- Throughput: sustained 3x normal token/sec, many short bursts
- Customer impact: critical downstream alerts delayed; sales execs escalating to our CEO

Can Redwood confirm whether this is a rate-limiter/quota/burst policy shift on your side? We need an emergency throttle lift or routing change while we triage. Attached: p95 chart and sampled request IDs.

Laura Nguyen
Head of Platform, HealthSync
laura@healthsync.com
attachments: healthsync_p95_latency.png (png), sample-reqs.txt (text)

From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Laura Nguyen <laura@healthsync.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throttling impacting inference pipelines (urgent)

Laura — thanks for the data. We're treating this as P1. Initial readout from observability shows a tenant-level burst window transition triggered safety valve enforcement; a stale burst-credit ledger caused overconservative throttling for tenants that ran multiple concurrent small-batch jobs.

Immediate actions we're taking now:
- Temporarily increase HealthSync burst allowance (15 min window) and lift tenant safety valve for 30 minutes while we gather traces.
- Route a fraction of their traffic to a dedicated small-pool (canary) to reduce interference.
- Engaging Serving and Rate team to pull KV cache heatmaps and throttler logs.

I'll loop Marissa for exec alignment and Grace for ops runbook. Expect a status update within 30 minutes.

Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
attachments: mitigation-runbook.md (md)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: ceo@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Throughput squeeze — board/customer flag

Team — quick situational note for executive awareness. HealthSync has escalated to their leadership; risk of public outage notification if we don't restore steady throughput. Priority asks: 1) confirm root cause (quota vs routing vs kernel-level stall), 2) approve 4-hour SLA exception & temporary quota/top-up for HS (requested in attached PDF), 3) coordinate a postmortem and customer-facing communication.

Preliminary findings from infra: burst-accounting reconciliation job missed a recent schema migration; credits were not consumed properly, which made the safety valve interpret near-steady traffic as repetitive bursts. Karthik, Markus — can you confirm if the schema drift is the only vector or if a deployment last night changed the burst window semantics?

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
attachments: sla-exception-request.pdf

From: Laura Nguyen <laura@healthsync.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: support@healthsync.com, cto@medisys.io
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throttling impacting inference pipelines (urgent)

Thanks for the fast triage. We saw 60% reduction in 429s after your temporary lift and routing change, but p95 latency remains ~1.1s for some endpoints (still above our SLO). We attached a short log snippet with request IDs that still show backpressure.

We need a conservative estimate of timing for a permanent fix and confirmation that this won't repeat during tomorrow's heavier batch window. If necessary, we are prepared to accept a temporary model-quantization fallback or reduced concurrency in the short term.

Laura
attachments: sample-reqs-still-erring.log

From: olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Final update: mitigation path and exec ask for HealthSync escalation

Summary:
- Root cause: a schema migration in the burst-accounting service (2026-10-03) changed timestamp normalization for short-lived tokens. This led to double-counting of bursts for multi-shard, small-batch clients. The safety valve logic then throttled those tenants aggressively.
- Impact: transient 429 spikes and elevated p95 for HealthSync; reduction after temporary top-up and routing canary.

Action plan (approved):
1) Permanent fix: rollback schema change and deploy corrected migration by 2026-10-10 02:00 UTC. Owners: Rate Team (Karthik) + Serving (Markus).
2) Preventative: add end-to-end migration test and a canary for burst-accounting (in CI). Owner: Grace (SRE).
3) Customer remediation: grant HealthSync a 4-hour quota top-up and formal SLA exception for Oct 7–9. Marissa to approve customer credit.
4) Short-term safety: document an emergency playbook for on-call to perform bounded burst lifts without global safety valve disable. Owner: Olga.

Ask for Execs: Please approve the SLA exception + one-time credit and confirm sign-off to communicate to HS leadership. Draft customer note attached for review.

Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
attachments: customer-note-draft.txt
